evidence: src/infrastructure/http/SubscriptionController.ts: create() only calls this.start.execute(body.customerId, body.plan, body.seats). This is pure delegation.
src/infrastructure/http/SubscriptionController.ts: resize() only calls this.changeSeats.execute(id, body.seats). It has no seat validation logic.
src/infrastructure/http/SubscriptionController.ts: cancel() takes body.reason and calls this.cancelSubscription.execute(id, reason). It has no cancellation policy.
The StartBody, SeatsBody and CancelBody interfaces are request DTO shapes, which belong in the transport layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This is an HTTP controller in the infrastructure layer, and it is only a thin transport adapter. It declares the request body shapes (StartBody, SeatsBody, CancelBody). Each of its three methods reads fields from a request body and passes them straight to an application use case (StartSubscription, ChangeSeats, CancelSubscription), then returns the result. It contains no business rules: no seat-limit checks, no plan validation, no cancellation policy. It also does no persistence and makes no domain decisions. All of its responsibilities fit the transport role of an infrastructure file.
